we have proposed a general lower risk bound for a class of shrink-age estimators in a general multivariate estimation framework, and we have deduced from it a new family of estimators that are good alternatives to existing ones.
we propose a lower risk bound for a class of shrinkages and deduce new shrinkages whose risk can be close to the lower risk bound near a chosen point and yet bounded.
we provide a lower bound for risk of shrinkage estimatores in a general statistical model, and we use it to propose new shrinkage estimators that are close to this bound and yet remain bounded.

a general multivariate estimationproblem and the construction of shrinkage estimator with good risk.
a general multivariate statistical estimation problem and a class of shrinkages estimators.

the positive-part James–Stein estimator is not the best shrinkage estimator in the sense that there exist estimators whose risk is arbitrarily close to the optimal bound and yet remain bounded.

the positive-part James–Stein estimator, although it has a risk which is uniformly better than the usual estimator, is not the best possible shrinkage estimator, even if the shrinkage factor is allowed to be random.

the James-Stein shrinkage estimators are not optimal in general, and that the positive part of the James-Steinstein estimator is a good alternative.
